clauses.statement: Quasi-definiteness iff unique monic lower-degree orthogonality at every order.
The canonical formal polynomials satisfy the three-term monic recurrence at every order, including its zero-order boundary.
The monic recurrence subdiagonal coefficients are nonzero at every positive order.
The squared integral form below degree n is positive definite iff there are at least n support points.
At every order up to support termination the monic lower-degree orthogonality problem has a unique solution.
The canonical family spans every bounded-degree polynomial space.
Before support termination every canonical squared norm is positive and distinct canonical orders are orthogonal.
For finite support, the terminal canonical polynomial is the support node polynomial and its squared norm is zero.
For a spectral measure, support cardinality is the Krylov grade and the canonical monic polynomial is the actual Lanczos charpoly.
The actual Lanczos polynomial-evaluation vector at a Gauss node is a Jacobi eigenvector.
Every chosen unit Jacobi eigenvector is its normalized evaluation vector up to a real sign.
The original-measure Gauss weight is the reciprocal sum of squared orthonormal-polynomial evaluations.
The first q orthonormal Lanczos polynomials are orthonormal for the actual mass-scaled Gauss rule.
Exactness below n+k is equivalent to integrated-cardinal weights and nodal orthogonality below k.
Gauss-degree exactness is equivalent to monic nodal orthogonality and the integrated-cardinal rule.
With more than n support points no n-node rule is exact through degree 2n.
The actual canonical Gauss rule exists, is positive, and is exact through degree 2n-1.
The first 2n moments identify every distinct-node n-atom rule with the actual Gauss rule, up to permutation.
The first 2q matrix moments uniquely identify the actual Lanczos Gauss rule, including exact grade termination.
For more than k+1 compact support points, the real monic diagonal coefficient lies strictly between the interval endpoints.
At positive orders the monic norm-ratio coefficient is positive and at most the largest squared endpoint.
Every actual Lanczos diagonal lies between the ambient smallest and largest Hermitian eigenvalues.
Every signed off-diagonal has magnitude at most the ambient spectral norm; canonical positive off-diagonals are positive and satisfy this upper bound before breakdown.
Actual Lanczos and canonical moment Jacobi eigenvalues are exactly the zeros of the canonical monic polynomial, and are simple.
Actual nonterminal Lanczos and general canonical Gauss nodes lie strictly between the active support extrema.
Consecutive actual Lanczos and canonical moment Jacobi spectra strictly interlace before termination.
A support-free open interval contains at most one actual Lanczos or canonical Gauss node, including finite-support termination.
Every normalized actual Lanczos Gauss weight and every original-measure canonical integrated-cardinal weight is strictly positive.
Every distinct-node interpolatory cardinal rule integrates all polynomials below its node count.
The actual moment construction gives distinct real roots of the canonical monic orthogonal polynomial.
The actual integrated-cardinal Gauss rule has positive weights, total mass, and degree-2n-1 exactness.
